description: Small concept-curriculum pilot for teaching the material affordance of stirring.
notes: This pilot is general affordance teaching, not EWoK item generation.
The stirred material should be central; tools and containers should be secondary.
Start with 20 documents so generated quality can be inspected before scaling.
Coverage reminder: an earlier draft missed gases/vapors and coarse loose aggregates; keep both as positive subtypes when scaling or porting this profile.

Gases/vapors cover stirred currents and mixing in air, steam, vapor, smoke, or controlled gas containers; loose aggregates cover gravel, ice cubes, beads, pasta, stones, and other chunks that tumble while each piece stays solid.

concept_profile.definition: To move a tool or hand through a loose, fluid, granular, suspended, or deformable material so the material circulates, shifts, or mixes.
concept_profile.centrality_rule: The stirred material must be the central participant; the document should not mainly teach about the tool, container, or person.

positive_subtypes.label: liquids
positive_subtypes.mechanism: liquids flow around the stirring tool and circulate in place

positive_subtypes.label: viscous liquids
positive_subtypes.mechanism: thick liquids resist motion but still deform and mix when pushed

positive_subtypes.label: slurries
positive_subtypes.mechanism: water and fine solids move together as a soft mixture

positive_subtypes.label: powders and grains
positive_subtypes.mechanism: many small pieces slide and rearrange around one another

positive_subtypes.label: loose chunks and aggregates
positive_subtypes.mechanism: loose solid pieces can be stirred because the chunks tumble, slide, and rearrange even though each piece stays solid

positive_subtypes.label: pastes and batters
positive_subtypes.mechanism: soft thick materials turn over and blend when pushed

positive_subtypes.label: soft unset gels and foams
positive_subtypes.mechanism: soft unset materials can be displaced and blended before they firm up

positive_subtypes.label: gases and vapors
positive_subtypes.mechanism: gases and vapors can be stirred or mixed by currents that make the material circulate and combine; fuel gases should only appear in sealed or controlled-container examples

negative_subtypes.label: rigid solids
negative_subtypes.reason: one solid piece does not circulate or mix under a stirring motion

negative_subtypes.label: sheets and fabrics
negative_subtypes.reason: a sheet bends, folds, hangs, or drapes instead of being stirred as a mixture

negative_subtypes.label: fixed structures
negative_subtypes.reason: fixed structures stay in place and cannot be mixed by a stirring motion

negative_subtypes.label: brittle solids
negative_subtypes.reason: brittle solids tend to crack or break rather than circulate

negative_subtypes.label: elastic single objects
negative_subtypes.reason: a single elastic object compresses or rebounds rather than mixing

state_contrasts.lesson: wet cement can be stirred before it sets; hardened cement cannot be stirred
melted chocolate can be stirred; a solid chocolate bar cannot be stirred
unset gelatin can be stirred; firm gelatin mostly jiggles or breaks
wet clay slip can be stirred; dried clay cannot be stirred
loose grains can be stirred; a packed block does not stir like a loose material

neighbors.label: mix
neighbors.relation: closest positive neighbor: stirring often causes mixing

neighbors.label: swirl
neighbors.relation: circular motion that may not fully combine materials

neighbors.label: shake
neighbors.relation: moves the container or object instead of moving a tool through the material

neighbors.label: pour
neighbors.relation: transfers material from one place to another instead of mixing in place

neighbors.label: knead
neighbors.relation: presses and folds dough-like material rather than stirring through it

neighbors.label: drape
neighbors.relation: fabric hangs over a surface instead of circulating as a mixture

neighbors.label: hang
neighbors.relation: an object is suspended rather than stirred

neighbors.label: squeeze
neighbors.relation: compresses material rather than circulating or mixing it

discourse_styles.description: A plain connective paragraph that places the target concept among nearby material behaviors.
guidance: Connect stirring to a larger family of material behaviors instead of giving only one isolated example.
Name 2-3 nearby actions when natural, such as mix, swirl, shake, pour, knead, drape, hang, or squeeze.
Explain why the target material fits stirring and why at least one nearby behavior has a different boundary.

discourse_styles.description: Brief, concrete observations of what happens before, during, or after an everyday material event.
guidance: Use plain observed changes instead of abstract labels.
Keep the material behavior visible: circulation, sliding, flowing, settling, bending, cracking, or staying fixed.

discourse_styles.description: Simple explanatory prose with child-friendly vocabulary and visible causes.
guidance: Use short, clear causal language.
Avoid dense terminology and microscopic mechanisms.

discourse_styles.description: A small ordinary scene where a person uses, prepares, notices, or changes a material.
guidance: Make the scene ordinary and concrete.
Keep the target material central rather than the person, tool, or container.

signal_orders.description: Start with the target affordance, then contrast with a negative or neighbor-winning case.
guidance: Lead with the material that fits the target action.
Then name a material, state, or neighbor action where the target action is not the best description.
Make the contrast explicit without turning the document into a quiz.

signal_orders.description: Start with the negative or neighbor-winning case, then explain the positive target affordance.
guidance: Lead with a material or state where the target action does not fit.
Then introduce the material that does fit the target action.
Use this order to reduce target-word-first bias.

signal_orders.description: Start by naming a nearby action that wins for another material, then contrast with the target action.
guidance: Begin with the neighbor action as the better description for one material.
Then explain why the target action fits the specified target material.
Keep both actions grounded in material behavior.

signal_orders.description: Start with the target action, then name the neighbor action that wins elsewhere.
guidance: Begin with the target action and the specified positive material.
Then name a neighbor action that is better for a different material or state.
Avoid implying the target action is the default for all materials.

signal_orders.description: Present two materials in parallel and assign different actions to each.
guidance: Use a parallel comparison of two materials or states.
Assign the target action to the material that supports it.
Assign a different neighbor action or response to the material that does not support it.
